**Question 1.** Which patient and hospital-stay factors best predict readmission within 30 days?

This document trains and compares three classifiers on the cleaned data from Part 1 (render
`01_data_preparation_eda.Rmd` first). The Python version is `python/02_q1_classification.ipynb`.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
# ---- Setup ----
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(rpart)
library(randomForest)
library(pROC)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)

# na.strings = "" keeps the 'None' test category as text
df <- read.csv("../data/processed/diabetes_clean_r.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")
dim(df)
cat(sprintf("30-day readmission rate: %.2f%%\n", mean(df$readmit_30) * 100))
```

# 1. Approach

The approach mirrors the Python version:

- **Features:** 25 predictors. The 7 numeric features are standardized; the 3 skewed visit counts
  (outpatient, emergency, inpatient) are log-transformed (`log(x + 1)`) and then standardized; the 15
  categorical features become factors, whose first level (alphabetically) is the reference in the
  logistic regression.
- **Imbalance:** only 8.98% of patients are readmitted. The logistic regression and decision tree weight
  each readmitted patient by the inverse class frequency; the random forest draws a balanced sample
  (equal numbers of readmitted and non-readmitted patients) for each tree. Accuracy is not used.
- **Metrics:** ROC-AUC (ranking quality), recall (share of readmissions flagged) and precision (share of
  flagged patients actually readmitted), at a 0.5 threshold.
- **Models:** logistic regression; a decision tree limited to depth 6 with at least 100 patients per
  leaf; and a random forest of 300 trees with at least 20 patients per leaf.
- **Validation:** an 80/20 split stratified on the outcome, plus 5-fold cross-validation on the training
  set.

```{r features}
num_cols  <- c("age_years", "time_in_hospital", "num_lab_procedures", "num_procedures",
               "num_medications", "number_diagnoses", "n_med_changes")
skew_cols <- c("number_outpatient", "number_emergency", "number_inpatient")
cat_cols  <- c("race", "gender", "admission_type", "discharge_to", "admission_source",
               "medical_specialty", "diag1_group", "diag2_group", "diag3_group", "A1Cresult",
               "max_glu_serum", "insulin", "metformin", "change", "diabetesMed")

data <- df[, c(num_cols, skew_cols, cat_cols)]
data[skew_cols] <- lapply(data[skew_cols], log1p)
data[cat_cols] <- lapply(data[cat_cols], factor)
data$readmit <- factor(df$readmit_30, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("no", "yes"))

# Stratified 80/20 split: sample 80% within each outcome class
set.seed(42)
idx_train <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(data)), data$readmit),
                           function(i) sample(i, round(0.8 * length(i)))))
train <- data[idx_train, ]
test  <- data[-idx_train, ]

# Standardize numeric features with the training means and standard deviations
scale_cols <- c(num_cols, skew_cols)
mu <- sapply(train[scale_cols], mean)
sdv <- sapply(train[scale_cols], sd)
train[scale_cols] <- sweep(sweep(train[scale_cols], 2, mu), 2, sdv, "/")
test[scale_cols]  <- sweep(sweep(test[scale_cols], 2, mu), 2, sdv, "/")

cat(sprintf("Training: %s patients (%.2f%% readmitted)\n", format(nrow(train), big.mark = ","),
            mean(train$readmit == "yes") * 100))
cat(sprintf("Test:     %s patients (%.2f%% readmitted)\n", format(nrow(test), big.mark = ","),
            mean(test$readmit == "yes") * 100))
```

# 2. Training and evaluation

```{r models}
# Class weights: each class contributes equally to the fit
class_weights <- function(y) ifelse(y == "yes", length(y) / (2 * sum(y == "yes")),
                                    length(y) / (2 * sum(y == "no")))

fit_predict <- function(model, tr, te) {
  w <- class_weights(tr$readmit)
  if (model == "Logistic regression") {
    # quasibinomial gives the same coefficients as binomial without warnings for non-integer weights
    fit <- glm(readmit ~ ., data = tr, family = quasibinomial, weights = w)
    p <- predict(fit, te, type = "response")
  } else if (model == "Decision tree") {
    fit <- rpart(readmit ~ ., data = tr, weights = w, method = "class",
                 control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 6, minbucket = 100, cp = 0))
    p <- predict(fit, te, type = "prob")[, "yes"]
  } else {
    n_yes <- sum(tr$readmit == "yes")
    fit <- randomForest(readmit ~ ., data = tr, ntree = 300, nodesize = 20,
                        strata = tr$readmit, sampsize = c(n_yes, n_yes))
    p <- predict(fit, te, type = "prob")[, "yes"]
  }
  list(fit = fit, p = p)
}

model_names <- c("Logistic regression", "Decision tree", "Random forest")

# 5-fold cross-validated ROC-AUC on the training set (stratified folds)
set.seed(42)
folds <- integer(nrow(train))
for (cl in c("no", "yes")) {
  i <- which(train$readmit == cl)
  folds[i] <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = length(i)))
}
cv_auc <- sapply(model_names, function(m) {
  sapply(1:5, function(k) {
    r <- fit_predict(m, train[folds != k, ], train[folds == k, ])
    as.numeric(auc(train$readmit[folds == k], r$p, levels = c("no", "yes"), direction = "<",
                   quiet = TRUE))
  })
})

# Fit on the full training set and evaluate on the test set
set.seed(42)
fits <- lapply(setNames(model_names, model_names), function(m) fit_predict(m, train, test))

results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(model_names, function(m) {
  p <- fits[[m]]$p
  pred <- ifelse(p >= 0.5, "yes", "no")
  tp <- sum(pred == "yes" & test$readmit == "yes")
  data.frame(model = m,
             cv_auc = sprintf("%.3f +/- %.3f", mean(cv_auc[, m]), sd(cv_auc[, m])),
             test_auc = round(as.numeric(auc(test$readmit, p, levels = c("no", "yes"),
                                             direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)), 3),
             recall = round(tp / sum(test$readmit == "yes"), 3),
             precision = round(tp / sum(pred == "yes"), 3),
             share_flagged = round(mean(pred == "yes"), 3))
}))
results
```

```{r roc, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 5.5}
roc_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(model_names, function(m) {
  r <- roc(test$readmit, fits[[m]]$p, levels = c("no", "yes"), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
  data.frame(model = sprintf("%s (AUC = %.3f)", m, as.numeric(r$auc)),
             fpr = 1 - r$specificities, tpr = r$sensitivities)
}))
ggplot(roc_df, aes(fpr, tpr, colour = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "ROC Curves on the Test Set", x = "False positive rate (1 − specificity)",
       y = "True positive rate (recall)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

```{r confusion}
for (m in model_names) {
  cat("\n", m, "\n")
  print(table(Actual = test$readmit, Predicted = ifelse(fits[[m]]$p >= 0.5, "yes", "no")))
}
```

**Interpretation.** All three models rank patients better than chance, with test ROC-AUC between
`r min(results$test_auc)` and `r max(results$test_auc)`; the cross-validated AUCs are similar, so the
comparison is stable. As in Python, the random forest and logistic regression rank best, and no model
reaches high precision: the best precision is `r max(results$precision)` against a 9% base rate.

# 3. Which factors matter?

## 3.1 Logistic regression: odds ratios

```{r odds}
coefs <- coef(fits[["Logistic regression"]]$fit)[-1]
odds <- data.frame(term = names(coefs), coefficient = coefs, odds_ratio = exp(coefs))
top <- odds[order(-abs(odds$coefficient)), ][1:12, ]

ggplot(top, aes(x = reorder(term, odds_ratio), y = odds_ratio, fill = odds_ratio > 1)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "firebrick", "FALSE" = "steelblue"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Logistic Regression: 12 Largest Effects (Odds Ratios)", x = "Term",
       y = "Odds ratio (>1 raises, <1 lowers readmission odds)")

data.frame(top[, -1], row.names = top$term) %>% round(3)
```

## 3.2 Random forest: permutation importance

```{r permutation}
# Drop in test ROC-AUC when one feature's values are shuffled (5 repeats)
rf <- fits[["Random forest"]]$fit
base_auc <- as.numeric(auc(test$readmit, fits[["Random forest"]]$p, levels = c("no", "yes"),
                           direction = "<", quiet = TRUE))
set.seed(42)
features <- c(num_cols, skew_cols, cat_cols)
drops <- sapply(features, function(f) {
  mean(replicate(5, {
    shuffled <- test
    shuffled[[f]] <- sample(shuffled[[f]])
    p <- predict(rf, shuffled, type = "prob")[, "yes"]
    base_auc - as.numeric(auc(test$readmit, p, levels = c("no", "yes"), direction = "<",
                              quiet = TRUE))
  }))
})
imp <- data.frame(feature = features, mean_auc_drop = round(drops, 4)) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_auc_drop))

ggplot(head(imp, 12), aes(x = reorder(feature, mean_auc_drop), y = mean_auc_drop)) +
  geom_col(fill = "seagreen") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Random Forest: Permutation Importance (Top 12)", x = "Feature",
       y = "Drop in test ROC-AUC when the feature is shuffled")

head(imp, 12)
```

## 3.3 Decision tree: the top splits

```{r tree}
# Splits are on standardized (and log-transformed) values
tree <- fits[["Decision tree"]]$fit
print(head(tree$frame[tree$frame$var != "<leaf>", c("var", "n")], 7))
```

```{r save}
write.csv(results, "../report/figures/q1_results_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(imp, "../report/figures/q1_permutation_importance_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# 4. Discussion

The R models reach the same conclusions as the Python version. **Discharge destination** is the most
important feature (shuffling it lowers the random forest's AUC by
`r imp$mean_auc_drop[imp$feature == "discharge_to"]`), followed by **prior inpatient visits**
(`r imp$mean_auc_drop[imp$feature == "number_inpatient"]`). In the logistic regression, being
discharged home has an odds ratio of
`r round(odds$odds_ratio[odds$term == "discharge_toHome"], 2)` against discharge to a care facility,
and each standard deviation of log inpatient visits has an odds ratio of
`r round(odds$odds_ratio[odds$term == "number_inpatient"], 2)`. The smaller effects of age, length of
stay, number of diagnoses and specialty also match.

The exact numbers differ slightly from Python because the train/test split is drawn by a different
random number generator, and the R random forest handles imbalance by balanced sampling rather than
class weights. The overall picture is the same: the models rank patients only moderately well
(ROC-AUC about 0.64–0.65), because much of what drives readmission happens after discharge and is not
in the data.
